About Event

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16–18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area’s deep-tech ecosystem.
Over 36 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers, and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges , with access to technical mentors, development hardware, and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.
Challenge Tracks
OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis - How do you stop one compromised system from taking down an entire ship?

Piping Layout Optimization - Can algorithms find better piping and cable layouts than traditional engineering workflows?

Software-Defined Vessel - What if ships could upgrade and change missions as easily as software platforms?

Agenda

4 PM - Registration opens
5 PM - Welcome remarks by Organizers
6 PM - Reveal of challenges
7 PM - Formation of teams & start hacking
8 PM - Dinner
Saturday, October 17
8 AM - Breakfast

3:00 PM - Award Ceremony

Build with Real Hardware
Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware, and supporting developer tools.
These tools are intended for hands-on technical development . Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision, or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.
Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors, or robotics into their prototypes.
Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.

Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.
👉 Join here: OFFICIAL DISCORD CHANNEL
More Than a 36-Hour Hackathon
The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.
Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.

Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team (Approximate Retail Value: $1,200 USD).

Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.

Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.

Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital, and the defense innovation ecosystem.

Partners & Ecosystem
The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri , Mind The Bridge and Silicon Mountain .
Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources, and technology expertise throughout the event.

Ecosystem Partners:

Berkeley Gateway Accelerator
Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance
Mission Applied Berkeley
Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation
SF Climate Tech Club
Bay Area Ocean Cluster
FLEETWERX
Hustle Hours
Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital, and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

Full details regarding participation rules, eligibility, and data privacy can be found in our Terms and Conditions .
What to Expect
36 hours of hands-on building and prototyping.

Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri.

Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources.

Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event.

Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers.

A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team.

Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts.

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon , and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design, or prototyping.
Come with a team or find one at the event.
Spots are limited — register early to secure your place. Registration will close on October 15.

Request to Join

About Event

Build it with OpenAI. Validate with Kane.
Kane CLI Hack Day SF, Supported by OpenAI.
Build it with an agent. Verify it with Kane.
Your agent can write an app in minutes. On October 24 you find out if that app actually works.
We're taking over a room in San Francisco for a full day of building with AI coding agents, with support from OpenAI. Kane CLI runs on OpenAI models under the hood, so for one Saturday the models that help write your code are also the ones checking it.
$30,000+ in prizes and credits
Saturday, October 24 · San Francisco · Hosted by TestMu AI, supported by OpenAI.
Seats are limited and every registration is reviewed. Apply early.
The Challenge
Build a working app with any AI coding agent. Use Kane CLI to prove it works. Ship by 6 PM.
That's all there is to it. Build a tool, a dashboard, a game, an internal utility, a strange experiment, or the side project that's been sitting in your notes app since spring. Just follow two rules:
Kane CLI has to verify your app. At minimum, run it at demo time. The teams that win will go further and put Kane inside the agent: a hook that runs Kane on every save, an agent that reads Kane's NDJSON output and keeps fixing until the flows pass, or a spec that compiles straight into Kane flows.

Your app has to run, ship and survive a live demo. Judges want to see it working in front of them.

Come solo or bring a team of up to four. Bring your laptop and your stack. We'll cover food, coffee, credits and help on the floor.
Pick your track
Web App: The fastest route from idea to verified. Kane CLI works on web apps right out of the box.

Mobile App: Build for iOS or Android and watch Kane test it on real devices through TestMu AI's device cloud.

Wildcard: Anything goes, as long as it ships and Kane can verify it.

Special Prize, Most Innovative Use of Kane CLI: For the team that does something with Kane that we didn't see coming.

The Prizes
🥇 1st Place: Apple Vision Pro + $3,000 in OpenAI credits

🥈 2nd Place: Apple Mac mini + $2,000 in OpenAI credits

🥉 3rd Place: Apple iPad + $1,000 in OpenAI credits

Every winning team also gets:
A 1:1 with the TestMu AI founders

Design partner status, with a say in the Kane CLI roadmap

A featured post on the TestMu blog

A spot on the Kane CLI showcase

A push across TestMu and dev.to channels

Every builder walks away with
$250 in OpenAI credits

3 months of KaneAI Pro (worth $270)

A full day of food, swag, and a room full of people shipping with agents

Before you arrive
Bring the agent you already use. CLI agents, IDE agents, chat agents, MCP setups or one you built yourself all work. Install it and sign in before you get here.

Install Kane CLI and run one flow. Run npm install -g @testmuai/kane-cli and try an example from the docs. A whole room running fresh npm installs at 10:05 AM costs everyone the first hour. Your confirmation email includes a cheat sheet.

Set up your OpenAI API account. Your confirmation email will explain how to claim your $250 in credits.

FAQs
Do I have to build with OpenAI? Participants receive $250 in OpenAI API credits.
Which AI agent should I use? Whichever one you already build with. Terminal agents, IDE agents, browser agents, custom agents, MCP servers and multi-agent setups all count. Kane CLI is the one required layer, and everything above it is your call.
Which other AI tools can I use? Anything that helps you ship. There's no approved-tools list, so bring your own models, frameworks and scaffolding.
Do I need a paid Kane CLI plan? No. Every builder gets 3 months of KaneAI Pro, starting on event day.
Can I bring a project I've already started? Yes, but the Kane CLI integration has to happen on the day. At demo time, show what existed at 10 AM and what you built after that. Judges will weight the new work.
Can I work solo? Absolutely. Solo builders are welcome, and so are teams of up to four.
Do I need to know Playwright or Selenium? No. Kane CLI works in plain English: describe the flow and Kane runs it. If you know Playwright, the built-in export is a nice bonus for your writeup.
What if my project breaks during demos? Test hard before 5 PM, because submissions lock at the deadline and you can't push fixes during demos. If your app depends on a third-party service, keep a recorded run or a backup deploy ready so judges still see what you built.

candidates.title: Universal Hackathon - Create Your Own AI Workforce | AWS Builder Loft
candidates.evidence:
Universal Hackathon - Create Your Own AI Workforce | AWS Builder Loft
Space is limited and is mandatory to register on https://events.builder.aws.com/EARgN9 (required to enter the AWS building) and join the discord: https://discord.gg/QF2AkaAfTr
All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs will not be accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building with no on-site parking available.
Exciting prizes of 10K+ in credits and cash

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building a prototype. It’s about imagining what a company looks like when AI agents can work together as a team.
The Challenge
Build a company run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business or startup where multiple specialized agents work together to build, operate, and grow the company.
Think of your agents as your founding team. You might have a CEO agent defining strategy, a product agent building the product, engineering agents writing code, marketing agents finding customers, sales agents closing deals, finance agents managing the business, and operations or customer-support agents keeping everything running.
The key question is:
What happens when you give an AI team a business to run?
What to Build
Build a working prototype of a company powered by a team of collaborating AI agents.
Your project should:
Identify a real problem or opportunity.
Define a clear product, service, or business.
Create multiple AI agents with distinct roles and responsibilities.
Show how your agents communicate, collaborate, and make decisions.
Demonstrate how the agents can actually execute business tasks.
Show how your company could acquire customers, deliver value, and grow.
You can build for consumers, businesses, creators, communities, or any other audience.
Don’t just build an AI feature. Build the beginnings of an AI-native company.
Tracks
Choose one or multiple tracks and build your company within them.
Climate, Sustainability & Impact
Build AI solutions for a healthier planet and stronger communities.
Examples: climate, sustainability, agriculture, disaster response, smart cities, social impact.
Health, Wellness & Care
Build AI solutions that improve health, wellbeing, and quality of life.
Examples: healthcare, fitness, nutrition, mental wellness, elder care.
Education, Learning & Research
Build AI solutions that make learning, education, and research better.
Examples: tutoring, personalized learning, professional training, research, career development.
Business, Growth & Productivity
Build AI solutions that help businesses work smarter, grow faster, and operate better.
Examples: sales, marketing, CRM, analytics, productivity, automation, business operations.
Media, Entertainment & Creators
Build AI solutions for creativity, entertainment, and digital experiences.
Examples: film, music, gaming, content creation, creator tools, social media.
Commerce, Retail & Consumer
Build AI solutions that transform how people shop and how businesses sell.
Examples: e-commerce, marketplaces, retail, logistics, inventory, personalized shopping.
Build the Future
Whether you're creating a climate startup, an AI health company, an education platform, a new media studio, or an autonomous business operating system, the goal is the same:
Build a company where a team of AI agents can turn an idea into reality.
Sponsors & Tools
Masky.AI

Masky.ai gives agents a face, voice, and brain. At the hackathon we'll give credits to clone yourself or bring your own characters to life. 

Then bring your agents into Maskord.com - discord for humans and agents. Connect agents built with your favorite coding harnesses and let your friends, teammates, and their agents all talk and work together in the same channels.

Aly will talk briefly about mental wellness and Living Book where she turned herself and her book into an interactive voice/avatar agent that creates audio and talks with fans online identifying social media posts and giving her notifications when people post content related to her focus. 

$800 in prizes awarded to teams that keep human communities safe as we bring this new intelligence online at scale. Agents should participate in human communities, not replace them. Masky is the place where the agent workforce becomes social.
Cognee
Cognee is an open-source AI memory and knowledge engine that helps applications organize, connect, and retrieve information from different data sources. Check out https://www.cognee.ai
N8N
N8n is a workflow automation platform that lets users connect apps, APIs, and AI tools to automate complex workflows with little or no code. Check out https://n8n.io
Synk
Snyk is a developer-first cybersecurity platform that helps teams build fast without compromising on security. As developers rely heavily on AI to write code at unprecedented speeds, Snyk continuously scans and secures application code, open-source dependencies, containers, and cloud environments right within the developer’s workflow. For an AI hackathon, it matters because shipping code quickly with AI generators or autonomous agents also means shipping security risks at machine speed. Snyk acts as an intelligent security layer, catching vulnerabilities and automatically applying verified fixes in real time—allowing builders to ship ambitious AI projects safely and with complete confidence.
At this event you will learn:
1) Sign-up for free (no credit card required), how to import your code, and configure your AI coding tool
2) Free AI Security Engineer Foundations Certificate
AdaL
AdaL is an automation-first agent harness designed to get more done with less of your time. She combines personality, skills, and memory to become a personalized agent that can work alongside you. Check out https://adalagent.ai
Tenki
Tenki provides sandbox environments, cloud compute, and runners for executing code and workloads. It gives builders a place to experiment, run, and scale their work. Check out https://tenki.cloud
Rocket Ride
Rocket Ride helps developers build AI and data pipelines directly in their IDE. It makes it easier to connect data, AI models, processing steps, and outputs into repeatable workflows. Check out https://cloud.rocketride.ai
Flatkey
Flatkey is a unified access layer for AI, connecting teams to 328+ official AI models through one API. It supports models from providers such as GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and more, with transparent pricing and automatic failover. Check out https://flatkey.app
Finch
Finch provides agent skills that give AI agents reusable capabilities for performing specific tasks. Skills can help make agents more useful, structured, and consistent. Check out https://www.finchtech.ai
Prelint
Prelint is your product whisperer, checking every pull request against product specs, business rules, and compliance requirements. It catches spec drift before code ships, turning product decisions into automated checks within your existing GitHub workflow so teams and AI agents can move fast without losing sight of what the product is supposed to do. Check out https://prelint.com
Paritok
Paritok drops in and non-destructively compresses tools, files, and history on the fly for longer sessions and smaller bills. Check out https://www.paritok.com
BAND
BAND helps AI agents and people work together in a shared environment. Its platform lets agents built with different tools communicate, delegate tasks, and keep context in sync, while giving teams visibility and control over how that work gets done. Check out https://www.band.ai
Kylon
Kylon helps you create AI agents that can run business processes. You can turn workflows into agents that understand tasks, use tools, and take actions. Check out

About Event

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.
READY TO BUILD?

If you're excited about the future of AI, agents and scientific discovery, we'll see you there...
We will close applications on Thursday, 30th of July, 12 PM PST. Spots will be confirmed on Friday, 31st of July.
WHO SHOULD ATTEND
People with the questions: scientists of all stripes. Wet lab, computational, clinical, industry. Biology, biochemistry, biophysics, chemistry, structural. Anyone with a real problem, ideally a real dataset, and the judgment to tell right from wrong results.
People who build for a living: ML engineers, software developers, and agent builders who can take a half-formed scientific problem and ship something that runs by Sunday.
No prior AI expertise required. Participants are welcome at all levels.

Tracks
Track A: Build an AI Scientist
Build an AI agent that can carry out a defined scientific or drug-development workflow from start to finish. It should gather evidence, use relevant tools or databases, generate and test hypotheses, produce a structured output, and make its reasoning easy to inspect. This could mean reasoning over experimental data, scientific literature, or learned representations like protein embeddings. Examples include a virtual FDA reviewer, toxicology agent, clinical trial designer, experimental planning agent, or a protein-discovery agent that generates and tests hypotheses over protein embeddings and structural features.
Track B: Build a Dataset or Meta-Analysis

What have you always wanted the literature to tell you, but could never read fast enough to find out? Draft the queries, run them across thousands of papers, sharpen and re-run until the results hold the specific pieces you care about. Then the real work: find the pattern in what you assembled that no single paper could show you, and demo that.
Track C: Build the Biological Design

Assemble a pipeline that designs biology to a spec you choose, from a single protein up to a multi-gene system. You set the constraints; the models generate candidates and evolve them toward something that could hold up in a real cell. Could the literature reveal the most promising design space for a generative model to explore? What you demo is the new biological design you made — the sequence or system that didn't exist before you built it.
Or come with a different project of your own.
Prizes will be awarded.

FAQs
Do I need a biology background or an AI background to participate?

No. We're looking for engineers with no life sciences experience as well as individuals who are in life sciences. One is helpful, but you don’t need both. The best teams usually pair technical builders with someone who knows the science.
Do I need a team before applying?
No. You can apply as a team, but you don’t have to. You can apply solo, and you'll meet potential teammates at the kickoff event.
What will I have access to during the hackathon?

Free Paperclip API access, access to Proto , Claude API credits, and compute and credits from our sponsors.
Is there a cost to attend?
The event is free to attend. Food, drinks, and compute are covered .
What happens to what I build afterward?

You keep it. Teams are free to open-source, continue building, or spin their project into something bigger.

About Event

A 10-hour hackathon where you go from a plain-English spec to firmware running on a real dev board, or to a computer vision model doing real-time inference on a GPU, using CraftifAI's AI agents for hardware engineers.
📅 Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026 · 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM PT
📍 San Francisco, CA
👤 Individual participation, no teams
🛠 ESP32 boards and sensors provided, cloud GPUs available.
🎒 Bring your own STM family board and sensors, or your NVIDIA Jetson, if you prefer
Why we're running this
AI coding agents changed how software gets shipped, but embedded and edge AI development have barely moved. If you've asked a general-purpose agent for an STM32 peripheral driver, you've probably watched the code compile fine and then fall over on the bench, because the agent guessed the clock tree or the pin mux. Vision pipelines go the same way. Ask twice and you get two different pipelines. One decodes video on the CPU and can't keep up with the camera. The other expects raw frames when your camera sends MJPEG. The agent can see what hardware it's on. It just doesn't know what actually works on it, so it guesses, and the guess changes every time.
CraftifAI builds agents that don't stop at a guess. FirmGen writes firmware for ESP32 and STM32 MCUs, then compiles it, flashes it to the board and debugs it there. PipeGen turns Python CV code and ONNX models into production-ready NVIDIA DeepStream apps, benchmarked on the GPU and packaged in a container. This hackathon is your chance to put both to the test on real hardware, in a single day.
Track 1 · FirmGen: Embedded Firmware
Describe the device you want to build, whether it's a robot subsystem, a wearable or a sensor node. FirmGen plans the firmware architecture, writes the drivers and application logic, then compiles, debugs and flashes it to the board on your desk. ESP32 family dev boards and matching sensors are provided on site. If you prefer to work on STM32, bring your own board and sensors, as we're only providing ESP32 family hardware.

FirmGen runs on Macs that meet these requirements:
macOS: 26 (Tahoe) or newer

Hardware: Apple Silicon only (M1 or later).

Disk space: About 8 GB free for the app and toolchain.

Bring: a laptop with a USB port. (If you don't have USB A port in your laptop , kindly get a USB hub).
Track 2 · PipeGen: Computer Vision & Edge AI
PipeGen & Edge MLOps: Computer Vision & Edge AI Describe what you want the camera to detect and what should happen when it does, whether it's counting people at a door, spotting a missing hard hat or flagging a car parked where it shouldn't be. PipeGen starts from an existing repo. It can pick the closest match from its catalog of use-case repos, work from one you bring, or use Deep Search to scan through repos and find the best fit. From there it builds the pipeline around your camera, measures how fast it runs and deploys it for real-time inference on your GPU. Need your own model? If nothing out there fits, train one with Edge MLOps. Bring labelled images or use one of its built-in public datasets.
Training runs on a Linux laptop with an NVIDIA GPU or on one of our cloud GPUs, not on a Jetson. Edge MLOps checks that the exported model gives the same results as the trained one, then hands it to PipeGen, which can still deploy it to your Jetson.
Participants working with PipeGen are encouraged to bring their NVIDIA GPU-enabled laptops to the event.
We’ll also provide cloud GPU access for up to 30 participants , available on a first-come, first-served basis . This will give teams additional compute capacity for building, testing, and running their Physical AI projects during the hackathon.
If you need access to a cloud GPU, make sure to claim your spot early.
Who should apply
Firmware and embedded engineers, robotics engineers, computer vision and perception engineers, and hardware founders who want to see how far AI agents can go on real hardware.
Pre-hack office hours
On Tuesday, Oct 12, 7:00 – 9:00 PM PT , accepted hackers join a live session with the CraftifAI engineering team to set up access, test their board or cloud GPU, and get technical questions answered before the day.

About CraftifAI
CraftifAI is building the AI engineering layer for physical products. Every robot, drone, smart camera and industrial controller runs on firmware and edge AI software that engineers still write by hand, against datasheets, board revisions and silicon constraints that general-purpose AI doesn't understand. Our mission is to give hardware engineers agents that reason about the hardware the way they do, so a working device is hours away instead of months.
Orbit, our platform, brings together FirmGen for firmware, PipeGen for computer vision and AgentIQ for FPGA design.

Challenge: Invisible Interfaces
The best interface is sometimes no interface at all. This edition explores products that work through voice, motion, sensors, live data, autonomous agents, and other natural interactions.
Build technology that helps people or systems sense, decide, and act without relying on a traditional app or screen.
1. Dispatch
Use live data such as ship traffic, flight data, fleet GPS, sensors, or border wait times to move physical things where they need to go.
Build for logistics, transportation, ports, emergency response, or defense.
2. No App
Build for people who will never open an app, including seniors, drivers, nurses, warehouse workers, and field crews.
Use voice, phone calls, glasses, vibration, or another invisible interface. If users have to look at a screen, it does not count.
3. Unsupervised
Build agents that run for hours without constant supervision.
Your system should know when it is stuck, overspending, looping, or when it needs to stop.

Build an AI-powered consumer product that reaches people through natural, ambient, or invisible interactions.
Rethink how people discover, use, and benefit from technology beyond traditional apps and screens. The strongest ideas will address a clear everyday need and have the potential to serve people at global scale.

What’s actually working for AI growth right now?
Building an AI product has never been easier. Getting real users, distribution, and revenue is still hard.
Local Align #3 is a hands-on day for people who want to learn how modern AI products actually grow — from SEO/GEO and organic content to developer growth, community, outbound, automation, and AI-powered GTM.
🎤 Learn from real growth stories.
Hear founders break down how they went from 0 → 1,000+ users , built communities of 10,000+ , and generated millions of organic impressions without relying on paid acquisition.

Choose from 5 real products with 5 different GTM problems — AI DevTools, consumer community, high-trust services, FinTech, and generative AI — and use AI, code, content, or automation to move real metrics: users, leads, signups, traffic, and conversions.

No generic startup advice. Hear real 0→1 growth stories from founders and operators who have built audiences, acquired users, and turned distribution into a system.
Lucy Ye — Co-founder & COO, JobWizard.ai
SEO/GEO × Organic Content × AI-Native Growth
Built a 0→1 SEO engine that generated 2M+ Google Search impressions in 2 months , plus 1M+ organic video impressions with zero paid acquisition . Learn how an early-stage AI startup turns search, content, and AI automation into repeatable distribution.
Weijia — Founder & CEO, LingCode
Developer Growth × Product-Led Growth × Community
Built content reaching millions, grew a coding education platform from 0 → 10,000+ students , and took LingCode from launch to 1,000+ users in its first month . Learn how technical founders can turn product, content, and community into an organic growth engine.
More founders & GTM operators to be announced.
⚡ Build: 5 Real Products. 5 Real Growth Problems.
Most hackathons ask you to build another demo.
Here, you'll work on a real product with real users and a real GTM problem — then use AI, code, content, outbound, SEO/GEO, automation, communities, or whatever else you can invent to move the numbers.
💻 AI Developer Tools — LingCode
How do you win developers when every week brings another AI coding tool?
Grow an AI-native IDE through developer communities, technical content, product-led loops, GEO, creators, or your own growth automation.
Learn: developer GTM, PLG, community growth, and how technical products earn adoption.
🎾 Consumer Community — Tennistry
3,500+ users. 1,500+ real tennis matches. How do you create the next 1,000?
Tennistry connects tennis players in real life. Test local acquisition, referrals, ambassadors, events, creators, and ways to prove which users you actually brought in.
Learn: consumer growth, network effects, referral loops, local/community GTM, and attribution.
🇺🇸 High-Trust Services — TurboNIW
How do you acquire customers when the decision is expensive, complex, and built on trust?
TurboNIW helps STEM researchers and professionals prepare for the EB-2 NIW process through structured educational materials and guidance. Unlike a casual app download, customers may spend $1,000+ and are making a high-stakes career decision—making trust and intent central to acquisition. TurboNIW
Learn: high-intent SEO/GEO, trust-based funnels, educational content, lead qualification, and customer acquisition for high-consideration services.
💳 Consumer FinTech — MaxWorth
30,000 users already. What becomes the next scalable growth channel?
MaxWorth is a North American credit-card management app entering its next stage of growth. Explore finance content, SEO/GEO, creators, referrals, communities, partnerships, or new product-led acquisition loops.
Learn: consumer FinTech GTM, lifecycle growth, referral mechanics, content distribution, and scaling beyond early adopters.
🎬 Generative AI × Entertainment — SxeneMixer
A new AI creative product is starting from zero. Where do the first 100 real users come from?
SxeneMixer is an AI short-drama generation platform. Find the creators and communities most likely to care, then experiment with UGC, viral formats, creator seeding, social distribution, and product-led sharing.
Learn: 0→1 launches, creator GTM, UGC, viral loops, and consumer AI distribution.

About Event

🚀Make an impact on real world problems in a single weekend!🚀
HSI is back for our third year in a row! Join Hack for Social Impact once again to tackle real-world challenges . We are teaming up with non-profit partners to present you with important and well-scoped challenges, in partnership with UN Convention to Combat Desertification and 4 local nonprofits.
This event is supported by our sponsors: Gemini, Bild.ai , and Wefunder. Developers will receive credits during the hackathon to work on your projects from our sponsors and technology partners.
$5000 cash prizes in total for the winners of projects
This year, we've teamed up with incredible partners to tackle pressing issues in mental health, climate, justice reform, and art & design:

🌎 Climate : Work with the UN to build an interactive game to enable the community to participate in land planning! Block by Block is a Minecraft-based tool for communities to design their own streets, and has run in 55 countries since 2012. However, it is unsuited to UNCCD's work in real-world land planning: Minecraft has endless resources, arbitrary terrain, and no consequence to player actions. Build a game from real satellite and GIS data showing the impact of land use, to engage the community.
🩷 Mental Health : Boundless Freedom Project can reach people inside with mindfulness and mental health practice through in-person sessions and the Edovo tablets. On release that support falls away, during the 30 days that hit hardest. Build something that keeps familiar practice at hand, holds as little personal information as possible, and assumes no smartphone and no dependable internet.
⚖️ Justice Reform : California's corrections department spends under one percent of its budget on rehabilitation. Transformative Programming Works advocates for them across 120 organizations, but so far can only track process data such as who enrolled and how long a class ran. Join disjoint records such as parole and recidivism data into a framework TPW, and nonprofits generally, can use to track impact.

🎨 Art & Design : BRIDGEGOOD's Oakland studio teaches designers to build with their own communities in mind, through conversations about identity, money and conflict that only work in a small room with a facilitator in it. That room seats a few dozen people a year. Find a way the practice can travel to designers who will never sit in it, without thinning into a slide deck.
🏆 Past winners went to present at UN Climate Conference and build startups that get accepted to YC and raise seed funding!🎯 Will your weekend hack be next year's success story?

HSI is back for our third year in a row! Join Hack for Social Impact once again to tackle real-world challenges. We are teaming up with non-profit partners to present you with important and well-scoped challenges, in partnership with UN Convention to Combat Desertification and 4 local nonprofits.

Request to Join

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Free 3-day Sprint for pre-seed founders. October 21 to 23, SAP Labs, Palo Alto.
Judges from Stanford, Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft AI spend three days watching how your team actually works, then question you on it. You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate, built for investor conversations.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures and join Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator.
20 team spots. Applications close Oct 14
Judges
Mohammad Rasouli Phd., Researcher, AI for Private Markets, Stanford
Sajal Garg, Principal Soft Eng, Microsoft AI
Abhinav Balasubramanian, AI Lead, Nvidia
Tharun Tej Tammineni, AI Lead, Meta
What this is
Judges who lead AI at Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft AI, and Stanford spend three days watching how your team works, then question you on it. They'll push on your build, your technical claims, and how your team decides. Better here than in a pitch meeting.
You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate. Evidence you can bring to investors, not a pitch deck you rehearsed.
Two tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no customer contact yet. For founders seriously exploring a startup, including people inside companies weighing the leap.
Pre-Seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what changed, pressure-test your next move.
What you get
No cash. No trophy. Something more useful.
Teams that clear the Sprint's scoring bar earn the Street Test : 30 days back in the real world, building with no event deadline and no audience, just you and the market. It's a bar, not a ranking. Every team that clears it gets in.
Teams that finish the Street Test receive a Proving Ground report card , a scored record of how you operated across both stages. It covers three things: whether customers are pulling (Pull), whether progress held up after the event (Momentum), and whether this team fits this problem (Founder Fit). It's yours - bring it to investors, accelerators, or a cofounder you're recruiting.
A hackathon ends when the event does. This doesn't.
Schedule
Wednesday, Oct 21: 9am to 8pm. Kickoff, building begins.
Thursday, Oct 22: 9am to 8pm. Full build day.
Friday, Oct 23: 9am to 4pm. Finals, live defense, deliberation, awards.
Who should apply
Pre-seed founders with live customer conversations.
Builders, product leaders, designers, and operators ready to test an idea for real.
University students: the commitment is all three days, Wednesday to Friday, 9am to close. Limited undergrad spots.

The next chapter of agentic infrastructure is memory, persistence, and self-evolving systems. After bringing builders together at .local NYC, we’re bringing the hackathon to San Francisco during SF Tech Week, with the MongoDB team and our partners, to tackle one of the hardest problems in agentic AI: building harnesses that can adapt, remember, and operate reliably in production. Agents stall in production without governance, memory, and security, so this is your chance to build the infrastructure that gets past that point. structuredEvent.description:
The next chapter of agentic infrastructure is memory, persistence, and self-evolving systems.

After bringing builders together at .local NYC, we’re bringing the hackathon to San Francisco during SF Tech Week, with the MongoDB team and our partners, to tackle one of the hardest problems in agentic AI: building harnesses that can adapt, remember, and operate reliably in production. Agents stall in production without governance, memory, and security, so this is your chance to build the infrastructure that gets past that point.

We’re looking for impactful projects built with MongoDB Atlas, including Atlas Agent Engine, our new platform for building, deploying, and governing agents in production. It gives you one foundation for execution, memory, and governance. It also provides long-term memory (semantic, episodic, taxonomic, and procedural), retrieval powered by Voyage AI.

Whether you’re building agents that adapt their own guardrails, systems that hold context across weeks-long tasks, or entirely new approaches to persistent agent memory, bring something that goes beyond the demo and gets to deployment.

Real AI. Real clusters. Built for SC26.
Coming to Chicago for Supercomputing 2026? Start the week by building.
The CIQ Supercomputing Local AI Hackathon brings together 20 teams for a deeply technical, hands-on AI build weekend immediately ahead of Supercomputing.
Each team will get access to two Lenovo ThinkStation PGXs—powered by the NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip —to use throughout the weekend, connected into a multi-node environment and orchestrated through Fuzzball .
The challenge: build a real AI workload that actually takes advantage of the full cluster.
✏️ How to Participate
This is an intermediate, technical hackathon built for the AI and HPC community coming to Chicago for SC26, limited to a maximum of 20 teams. Once we reach capacity, additional applicants will be placed on a waitlist and notified if a spot becomes available.
Application Guidelines:
You must be able to attend the event in person.

Technical Expertise: Experience working with multi-node systems and HPC environments. No prior Fuzzball experience is required ; onboarding support will be provided.

Team Size: Minimum 3 members, maximum 5 members.

Priority: Full team applications will be prioritized over individual applications. We highly encourage you to form and apply as a team.

Individuals: If you apply as an individual, team formation will happen the first day of the event. If accepted, you will be required to compete with your assigned team.

🔥 Challenge Tracks
Over one weekend, teams will build, benchmark, and demonstrate an AI or HPC workload running across their multi-node cluster.
By Sunday, your team should be able to demonstrate both what you built and what the additional compute actually unlocked.
🕸️ 1. Multi-Node Training
Build a training or fine-tuning workload that takes advantage of compute across multiple nodes.
🚀 2. Inference at Scale
Explore multi-node inference for greater throughput, concurrency, model capacity, or performance.
🔬 3. Scientific AI
Apply distributed AI and accelerated computing to a scientific or research workload.
⚙️ 4. Cluster & Scheduling
Build around orchestration, scheduling, resource allocation, utilization, or multi-node infrastructure.

We're sending the top 3 teams straight from the hackathon into Supercomputing 2026.

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.

About Event

Join us for the Patch the Conference Hackathon, right before GitHub Universe, where we're looking for builders who can find what's broken about conferences and ship the patch. If something about conferences has ever bugged you, this is your chance to build the fix.
Winners take away iPhone Duos, and there are more cool prizes that we'll announce soon. There's plenty of swag for everyone, plus free OpenAI credits to build with.
🗓️ Agenda
9:00 AM: Doors open

9:00 AM to 10:00 AM: Grab breakfast, get set up, start hacking and get familiar with the tools

10:00 AM to 11:00 AM: Workshops and talks from our sponsors to get you up and running

11:00 AM to 2:00 PM: Back to building

2:00 PM: Pizzas arrive, lunch is served

2:00 PM to 6:00 PM: Keep hacking and submit your project

6:00 PM to 7:00 PM: Judging, with teams showcasing their projects on stage

7:00 PM: Winners announced and the iPhone Duos handed over

🛠️ Tools
FalkorDB
FalkorDB is an open-source graph database built for AI agents. Agents are only as good as the context they work with, and a graph gives yours connected data it can reason over, a memory it keeps between sessions, and a clear picture of how things relate.
Here is how you can use it in your project:
Follow connections across data: let your agent answer questions that take more than one hop, with graph queries as its tools.

Remember across sessions: store conversation history and what the agent has learned, so it picks up where it left off.

Share state between agents: give multiple agents one graph to read and write, so handoffs between them work.

Follow connections across data: let your agent answer questions that take more than one hop, with graph queries as its tools.

About Event

Yummy Future Hackathon Festival
Presented by Yummy Future · Sponsored by AWS
📅 October 23–25, 2026
📍 South Bay + Online Worldwide
☕ Sip. 🤝 Meet. 🛠️ Build. 🏆 Compete.
Your next teammate might be one coffee away.
For three days, Yummy Future brings together the energy of a café, the curiosity of a demo floor, and the excitement of a hackathon. Explore new tools, meet the people behind them, collect Mission Card stamps, and turn a useful idea into something you can show.
Come with a team or find one here. Bring a problem from work, your neighborhood, or everyday life. Local businesses are welcome to share the challenges they would love someone to solve.
Join us in the South Bay—or build alongside us from anywhere in the world.
🎟️ Your Mission Card: A Festival Passport
Pick up your Mission Card at check-in and make your way through the café: meet people at the challenge boards, ask a question at a sponsor station, share what you are building, and collect stamps as you complete your missions.
Every stamp marks a step from “I just arrived” to “Look what we made.”
Here is how the planned on-site missions work:
Day 1 · Find Your People 🤝
Check in, complete your participant profile, and collect your badge → unlock your Coffee Pass .

Complete a verified team-matching action and update your status → unlock your Food Pass .

Register your team, choose a challenge, and submit your one-line idea → qualify for the announced sponsor gift or prize-draw activity.

Day 2 · Make It Work 🛠️
Check in and share your team’s daily plan → unlock your Coffee Pass .

Show a working prototype, meaningful code, an API integration, or another verified build milestone → unlock your Food Pass .

Complete a sponsor integration or put mentor advice into practice → work toward sponsor rewards. Share a 60-second progress video or join a scheduled team interview for additional reward opportunities.

Day 3 · Show What You Made 🏁
Check in and complete your final submission → unlock your Coffee Pass .

Pass your technical check and join your judging room on time → unlock your Food Pass .

Complete your final demo → finish your last mission and qualify for the announced sponsor gift.

Meet someone. Try something. Show your progress. Earn your next unlock.
Mission rewards require staff verification. Menus, quantities, sponsor gifts, and any prize-draw rules will be announced before the event.
🤝 Sponsor Office Hours Throughout the Day
Have a question you would normally leave unanswered? Bring it straight to the people behind the product.
The festival will feature a rolling program of Office Hours across participating sponsor companies during event hours. Each sponsor will have scheduled support slots, with café meeting points and Zoom access for remote participants.
You can:
Explore a product or API through a live walkthrough.

Ask about a challenge, integration, or technical blocker.

Join a short team consultation to work through your next step.

Take that advice back to your build—and turn it into your next Mission Card milestone.

Check the sponsor boards for times and scan the QR code to join the queue. Public Q&A sessions will be recorded; individual team consultations stay private unless the team agrees otherwise.
📺 Live Demos, All Day Long
There is something to follow throughout the event day: sponsor product demos, quick project showcases, team progress updates, and conversations with the people doing the building.
Watch on the café screens, join a scheduled show-and-tell segment, or follow online. Public segments will be livestreamed and recorded, with replays and highlights capturing how projects develop across the weekend.
The early demos are a chance to share work in progress. Sunday’s finalist demos are where teams compete for the awards.
🏆 Chase the Grand Prize
Take your project from a whiteboard conversation to a live demo—and compete for the grand prize.
The planned awards program also includes sponsor challenge awards, recognizing how teams turn technology into useful solutions.
Grand prize details, sponsor prizes, and final award categories are coming soon.
Judges will look at the problem you solve, product execution, originality, meaningful technology integration, business potential, and the clarity of your demo.
🗓️ Your Three-Day Plan
Friday, October 23 · Meet, Match & Get Started
Morning: Check in, pick up your Mission Card, and join the opening and sponsor challenge briefings.
Midday: Explore the Idea Marketplace. Give a 30-second pitch: what do you want to build, and who would you love to build it with? Find collaborators at the challenge and team-matching boards.
Afternoon: Join sponsor Office Hours, explore live demos, and work through your first missions.
Evening: Get mentor feedback, confirm your team and challenge, and register your project idea.
Saturday, October 24 · Build, Play & Make Progress
Morning: Share your team’s daily plan, unlock your coffee, and start building.
Throughout the day: Move between focused build time, sponsor Office Hours, live demos, and mentor sessions. Test your prototype, ask for help, and share a quick progress update.
Afternoon and evening: Show a verified milestone to complete your food mission. Check your integrations and prepare your submission, slides, and backup demo video.
Sunday, October 25 · Submit, Demo & Celebrate
Morning: Complete your final submission before the published deadline, test your demo setup, and take part in preliminary judging.
Afternoon: Selected finalists present live to the judges, with on-site and remote teams joining the same demo program.
Closing: Grand prize and sponsor award announcements, a celebration of the projects, and the final Mission Card milestones.
Exact session times, the event time zone, and submission deadlines will be announced before kickoff.
🌍 A Global Festival, With a South Bay Home
Online participants can join team matching, sponsor briefings, Office Hours, and the competition. Remote ideas and teammate requests will also appear on the café’s matching boards, helping people connect across locations.
Everyone follows the same submission deadline and judging criteria. Replays and shared FAQs help participants catch up across time zones; finalists present through the shared Zoom demo room.
Coffee and food missions are part of the on-site café experience.
🚀 Ready to Join?
Register and choose in-person or online participation.

Complete your profile so teammates can find you.

Join a team and choose a challenge.

Build and submit: your project summary, team details, product and repository links, required integration evidence, a short slide deck, and a 2–3 minute backup demo video.

The proposed finalist format is 2 minutes to pitch + 2 minutes to demo + 2 minutes of judge Q&A .
Bring your laptop, charger, and curiosity. Joining remotely? Have headphones, reliable internet, and screen sharing ready. Venue details, joining links, and final competition rules will be shared through the event hub.
Come for the coffee. Find your team. Make something worth showing.

About Event

📍 Ctrl+Space San Francisco: join us in person
This is the San Francisco in-person event for Ctrl+Space , the global online hackathon from ReactVision and Expo. Come meet other builders, hack together and celebrate the best projects.
How to take part
Register for the online hackathon. You need this to compete: luma.com/ctrl_space

Join the Discord. Announcements, team formation, help and the submission form all live there: Join Discord Server

Pick your track. Code (ViroReact + Expo) or no-code (ReactVision Studio). Rules and setup are in #hack-rules-faq.

Build during build week, Oct 3–11. Submissions close Sun Oct 11, 11:59 PM PT . A 2–4 minute demo video is required.

Celebrate in person. Top teams will be invited to an in-person celebration and prize distribution.

Key dates (Pacific time)

Daily office hours, Oct 5–10, on the Discord stage

Finalists announced: Wed Oct 14

Virtual finals livestream: Thu Oct 15, 9–11 AM PT ( RSVP )

The venue address is shared with approved guests. Space is limited.
Build a real AR/VR app with React Native - no Unity, no native rewrite, just the stack you already know.
ReactVision and Expo are teaming up for a hackathon built for developers who want to go past the demo stage. One fixed build week, four cities, real judges, and a direct path into Expo's App Awards if you ship something worth entering.
We're looking for real AR/VR depth: geospatial anchoring, cross-platform native builds, spatial experiences that actually work in the physical world. Bring an idea, bring a team (or fly solo), and build something that runs on iOS, Android, and Quest from one codebase.
🎮 Details
Who can participate: All skill levels welcome · Individuals & teams (up to 4)
Open globally, in-person events in SF, London, Bengaluru and Toronto
📅 Build Week: Oct 3–11, 2026
📍 Format: Global, virtual build week + in-person regional finals
🏆 4 prize tiers · Guaranteed perks for all participants
Ctrl+Space is a joint hackathon between ReactVision and Expo, focused on building real AR/VR experiences using React Native : no Unity, no native rewrites, no starting from scratch.
This hackathon invites developers, designers, and builders to create next-generation spatial computing experiences across industries like education, real estate, retail, training, and enterprise.
✨ What Makes Ctrl+Space Special
🌐 Focus on real spatial computing : geospatial anchors, cloud anchors, and genuine device-agnostic builds, not surface-level AR effects
🧠 Build with code (ViroReact + MCP server) or no-code (ReactVision Studio) : pick the path that fits you
🤝 Open for both solo participants and teams
🚀 Direct eligibility for Expo's App Awards if you ship something real
🛠 What You Can Build
You can create:
AR/VR experiences using ViroReact, ReactVision Studio, or the MCP server

Geospatial or Cloud Anchor–based experiences : persistent, real-world-anchored, not single-session

Cross-platform builds : one codebase shipping to phone and Wearables alike

Spatial training, education, or simulation experiences

Agent-built apps : use an AI coding agent connected to the ViroReact MCP server to scaffold and validate your scene

Infrastructure or tooling that uses Expo's build/deploy stack alongside ReactVision

🎯 Important Creation Guidelines
To ensure quality and consistency across submissions:
Build your AR/VR experience using ViroReact, Studio, or the MCP server

For education or training use cases: include a clear walkthrough (voiceover or on-screen explanation) so judges understand the concept

For other use cases (retail, real estate, enterprise, etc.): show the experience running and interacting in a real environment, not just a static render

⚠️ Important Note
🚫 Submissions without a demo video will NOT be considered

Also share on social media and tag @reactvision and #Ctrl+Space

Requirements
📦 Submission Requirements
To submit a valid project, include:
🔹 Basic Details
Project Title & Description

Problem Statement

Solution Overview

Target Users / Industry

🎥 Demo Video (Mandatory – 2–4 mins)
Your video must clearly explain:
What you built

How it works

Why it matters

🖼 Additional Assets
Screenshots / Images (at least 2)

Tech Stack Used

GitHub / Source Code Link

Platform Details (iOS, Android, Meta Quest, or Web)

Prizes
1st Place – Grand Winner : 1 team
Featured case study on ReactVision + Expo channels

Direct eligibility for Expo App Awards

1-year ReactVision Pro tier + 1-year Expo credits

2nd Place : 1 team
6-month ReactVision Pro tier + 1-year Expo credits

Runner-up feature on our channels

3rd Place : 1 team
1-year ReactVision Basic tier + 1-year Expo credits

All Participants
Free ReactVision Studio access

1-month Expo Starter plan upgrade

Access to the shared Expo × ReactVision Discord

Judges from
ReactVision

Expo

Meta

Pico

Judging Criteria
Innovation & Creativity: Originality of the idea and uniqueness of approach to the problem space.
Technical Implementation: Effective, skillful use of ViroReact, Studio, geospatial/cloud anchors, or the MCP server.
Real-World Impact: Applicability to a real industry or use case : not just a technical demo.
Design & Experience: Immersion quality, usability, and how the interaction actually feels.
Presentation & Demo Quality: Is the demo video clear, concise, and does it actually prove the thing works?

candidates.evidence:
AboutHackathonAgendaSpeakersVenueSponsorsVolunteersFAQContactRegister
AboutHackathonAgendaSpeakersVenueSponsorsVolunteersFAQContactRegister for free

October 13, 2026 · AWS Builder Loft

← AWS Community Day 2026

Agentic AI Hackathon

Participant Guide

Build an agent that does real work on AWS.

Two weeks. One track. Eight teams demo live on stage at AWS Community Day in front of 200+ builders. Up to $3,200 in AWS credits on the line.

Build window: Tuesday, September 29 to Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Submissions due: Sunday, October 11, 11:59 PM PT
Finals: AWS Community Day, AI Edition, October 13, 2026, AWS Builder Loft, 525 Market St, Floor 2, San Francisco, CA 94105
Teams and announcements: the hackathon Slack channel. The invite and channel links are in your kickoff email.
Questions: Ask in the Slack channel so everyone gets the answer, or use Contact the Host on the Luma page for anything private. Replies within 24 hours.
The challenge: Hand it off

Build an agent that takes over a task a specific person does by hand every week, and produces something that person would accept without redoing it.

Three requirements, and judges will check all three:

Name the person. A real role, not a persona: a clinic scheduler, an on-call SRE, a landlord with twelve units. Your writeup says who they are and what the task costs them today.
Call at least one tool you didn't build. An AWS service via tool use, a public API, or an MCP server. The agent has to act, not just talk.
Show the failure path. Your demo video shows what happens when that tool fails, returns garbage, or disagrees with the model. Happy path only is a demo, not an agent.

Everything else is open: domain, model, framework, number of agents.

What this is not: a chatbot with a nice UI, a RAG app that answers questions about documents, or a pipeline where a human still does the last step.

No project yet? Eight starter ideas that already meet all three requirements are posted in the Slack channel. Pick one, adapt it, or bring your own, and choose a lead by end of day Friday, October 2.

Two weeks is enough for a working prototype, not a finished product. Judges know that. Scope accordingly.

Your team
Registration closed on September 28 and teams are formed. Team assignments are posted in the hackathon Slack channel.
Teams are capped at 4. Solo registrants are matched by project theme, and each team has a lead: the person who brought the idea.
Find your team, email your teammates, and create a channel named #hack-<your team>, for example #hack-s07. If you can't reach someone by Friday, October 2, DM the hackathon lead and you will be reassigned.
You must be registered for AWS Community Day. Finalists present in person, and you can't be called on stage without it.
Organizers, judges, and their immediate work teammates can't win prizes.
Not registered for Community Day yet? Register here, it is free.
Rules
All hackathon work starts on or after September 29, when the kickoff email went out. Open-source libraries and frameworks are fine. Renaming an existing project is not.
Your project must meet all three challenge requirements above.
Use at least two AWS services, and at least one must be an AI service: Bedrock, AgentCore, Strands, SageMaker, Transcribe, Rekognition, and similar all count.
Your code must be in a public GitHub repo. Private repos, invite-only links, and zip files will not be accepted. The repo must be public at the time you submit and stay public through October 13. License it MIT or Apache 2.0.
No production customer data, PHI, or PII. Use synthetic or public datasets.
You own your IP. We just want to see it.
Be kind. The event code of conduct applies to every channel and the day itself.
Timeline
Date	What happensMon Sep 28	Registration closed.
Tue Sep 29	Hackathon starts. Kickoff email goes out with team assignments, the challenge and the rules. Build begins.
Fri Oct 2	Teams without a project pick one and choose a lead. Teammates who can't be reached get reassigned.
Mon Oct 5	Submission form and writeup template posted in the Slack channel.
Sep 29 to Oct 11	Build. Questions go in the hackathon Slack channel.
Sun Oct 11, 11:59 PM PT	Submissions due. No extensions.
Mon Oct 12 by 6 PM PT	Finalists notified by email.
Tue Oct 13	Community Day. Finalists check in at the hackathon room, dry-run on the main stage over lunch, demo live at 4:15 PM after the closing remarks. Winners announced right after the last demo.
How to submit

By Sunday, October 11, 11:59 PM PT, submit via the submission form. The four items below won't change, so build toward them now.

Public GitHub repo (MIT or Apache 2.0) with a README that runs. We open the link logged out; if it 404s, it doesn't count.
3-minute demo video, YouTube unlisted or Loom. Include the failure path. This is also your backup if the live demo fails, so make it good.
One-page writeup using the template: who the person is, what the task costs them today, an architecture diagram, AWS services used, and what you'd build next.
Team roster with names and emails. This is how credits get issued, so get it right. No roster changes after the deadline.

Download the writeup template (Word) → Fill in every section, keep it to one page, and export it as a PDF for the submission form.

Submit your project

Due Sunday, October 11, 11:59 PM PT. One submission per team; the lead submits.

How you'll be judged

Every criterion is scored 1 to 5 by each judge.

Technical depth

A 5 looks like: Real agentic behavior (planning, tool use, memory), sound AWS architecture, more than a prompt wrapper

Real-world usefulness

A 5 looks like: Solves a problem a real user has, clear target user, plausible path to adoption

Responsible AI

A 5 looks like: Guardrails, handles failure and hallucination, considers privacy and misuse, cites data sources

Demo and communication

A 5 looks like: Works live, tells a clear story, honest about limitations

Completeness and polish

A 5 looks like: Runs from the README, has tests or evals, clean repo

Round 1 (Oct 12): Judges score every submission asynchronously from your video, repo, and writeup. The top 8 become finalists.

Round 2 (Oct 13): Finalists demo live and are re-scored. You get 5 minutes, hard stop, with a visible timer. Judges may ask a quick question or two in the 1-minute changeover.

Judges decide right after the eighth demo and the winners are announced on stage before the room empties, around 5:00 PM.

Prizes
Winning team: $2,000 in AWS credits ($500 per member, up to 4 members)
Runner-up team: $1,200 in AWS credits ($300 per member, up to 4 members)

All 8 finalists get their demo recorded and featured on the AWS Community Bay Area YouTube channel, plus a shout-out from the organizers on LinkedIn.

Credits are AWS promotional credits applied to your own AWS account, issued within about two weeks after the event. Make sure every team member has an AWS account in their own name. Promotional credits typically have an expiry date and some service restrictions; we'll share the exact terms when codes are issued.

Finalist day-of checklist (Oct 13)
Arrive when doors open at 9:30 AM and check in at the hackathon room (the Track B room, yours until 2:00 PM).
Do the mandatory dry run with a volunteer on the main stage during lunch, 1:00 to 2:00 PM. Every team, no exceptions.
Bring your own laptop, charger, and any adapters. We'll have HDMI and USB-C at the stage.
Have your backup video open in a tab.
Practice the 5-minute version. Then practice the 4-minute version.
Tips from the organizers
Pick the demo moment first, then build backward from it.
A narrow agent that reliably does one thing beats a broad agent that sometimes does five.
Show the failure handling. Judges love seeing what happens when the tool call errors out.
Ask early. Nobody has ever regretted posting a question in the channel on October 3 instead of discovering the problem on October 11.

See you on stage October 13.

About Event

Build what a single model cannot.
The next generation of AI products will not come from picking one model. It will come from knowing which models, agents, and modalities to bring together for a real task, then making the system work.
With the release of "system one" models like Jev that enable fast tool calling and model selection, developers have the ability to use multiple models that may generate different modalities of output such as video, audio, image, or classifier, to build applications that were previously difficult, expensive, and slow.
For SF Tech Week, BuilderBase, Actual AI, Women in AI, and AI Collective are bringing builders together at Frontier Tower for a full day of building, testing, and live demos.
The challenge
Build an AI product that becomes more useful because it combines more than one model, provider, agent, or modality. Use the right system for each job: reasoning, code, vision, voice, long context, fast inference, or whatever your product needs. Put them together with intelligent routing that can choose models based on modality, speed, and cost to achieve a goal.
Build something a real person would use. By the end of the day, show what it does, why one model would not have been enough, and what the combination unlocks.
Who should join
Engineers, AI practitioners, designers, and technical founders who want to build something real in a day. No prior hackathon experience required. Bring a laptop, a problem you care about, or the willingness to join a team and start building.
Sponsors
Anbaric
Anbaric builds workflows that combine human steps, agentic steps and coded steps; we don't believe in a world where humans are replaced by AI, but, rather, the AI unlocks human time and creativity by automating boring admin that fills our days.
Base44
Base44 is a no-code AI development platform that turns builders' ideas into fully functional apps and websites — no coding required.
Actual AI
Actual AI manages Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) in your codebase to ensure your agent writes the right code first time, no matter how large the codebase.
Prelint
Your AI makes decisions. Prelint keeps every decision reviewed, recorded, and traceable. Every pull request gets a 20-second decision review.
Swytchcode
Legacy APIs and AI agents don't blend. Swytchcode gives agents the implementation knowledge these APIs never documented, then governs every action that runs.
Community Partners
Women in AI
Women in AI connects, empowers, and elevates female founders, investors, and engineers shaping the future of artificial intelligence. Through community, mentorship, and global events, we’re building a more inclusive AI ecosystem where women lead and innovate.

Julian Bryant is a San Diego attorney and software developer who uses AI in his own legal practice every day. A Georgetown Law graduate, Cooley alum, and former startup founder with a decade of app development behind him, he brings a rare blend of legal and technical fluency to the question of what AI can actually do for lawyers. About Event

On-Device AI Hackathon: Cleared for Takeoff ✈️
What if you could build an AI application that works, even when the Wi-Fi doesn't?
Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.
In this hands-on hackathon from Qualcomm × Liquid AI , you'll team up with a flight crew of up to four people to build with Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) and Qualcomm iQ9s. At the end of the night, we'll turn off the Wi-Fi and put every project to the test.
Will your project survive offline?
Why on-device AI?
Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴

Who this is for
👨‍💻 Developers who want to ship AI features without an inference bill

🤖 ML and AI engineers curious about deploying models beyond the cloud

⚙️ Edge, embedded, and robotics engineers building against real hardware constraints

🚀 Founders and product managers evaluating on-device versus cloud AI

🎓 Students and self-taught builders who want to leave having built something real

You don't need previous on-device development experience. If you can run a script, you can join the flight.
Teams may have up to four people . You can arrive with a team or meet your crew at the event.

It's time: Voice coding technology is now good enough. Openbase is hosting its third OUTDOORS hackathon as part of SF Tech Week, joined by Maritime and Sundai Club. Let's build apps, startups, and technology while enjoying nature and the outdoors at Stanford's beautiful campus, with minimal screens involved. It's the weekend, after all. Use Openbase (tool of choice) or your own home-grown solution to direct coding agents from your phone by voice (speech-to-speech preferred). No laptop? No problem. Openbase+Maritime offer cloud hosting solutions accessible via the Openbase app or Maritime website. Come as you are, no team needed, and meet others interested in innovating with voice AI. This hack is not only about *what* you make but also *where* and *how* you make it. Example projects from past hacks, done all made through voice: - Orchestrate a GTM agentic team and keep them running in loops - Building mobile command centers for visualizing agentic activity (with an audio-only agent-actvitiy radio station) - Knowledge curation: mine data from Whatsapp, Calendar, etc. and organize it in an Obsidean vault. - Location-based guided audio tours Who should join? About Event

Students, builders, founders, and climate-minded problem solvers are coming together during Stanford Climate Week for a fast-moving weekend of ideas, prototypes, and building.
Co-hosted by Stanford Climate Week & Raisable Founders Hub and sponsored by TotalEnergies and Google Earth (with more sponsors to be announced soon), the cleantech hackathon takes place in the Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center for two days of hacking.

Teams will build cleantech solutions with the potential to make a real difference by focusing on vetted business challenges from our sponsors and the Stanford Sustainability Accelerator.
Come with a team or find one at the event. Either way, expect a room full of ambitious thinking, hands-on building, and enough time to turn a spark of an idea into something tangible.

🔗 Hackathon guide: Coming soon
Think big, move fast, and spend two days building in the heart of Stanford.

Stanford Climate Week is a dynamic, interdisciplinary gathering that unites students, faculty, alumni, and industry leaders to drive climate action & innovation.
Raisable Founders Hub
Raisable Founders Hub is a community that supports founders while also building, designing, and leading innovation events like hackathons and accelerators. We connect founders with the sponsors, mentors, and programming they need to scale, and we're proud to bring that same builder-first energy to the Stanford Cleantech Hackathon.

Phase 1 — Build Day In Person | 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM Build 3 to 5 specialized AI agents across areas such as: Product Research GTM Sales Marketing Strategy Your agents should work together through real workflows, not operate as standalone chatbots. 12:00 – 1:00 | Kickoff & Sponsor Demos Challenge briefing Sponsor tool demos Team setup and Q&A 1:00 – 5:00 | Build SprintBuild the foundation of your startup: Identify and validate a problem Build a simple working MVP Create your initial AI agents Define your business model and GTM Prepare your demo and pitch 5:00 – 6:00 | JudgingDemo your startup and pitch to judges. Phase 1 prizes are awarded after judging. Completion of Phase 1 is required to continue to Phase 2. Phase 2 — Build the Zero Human Company October 7–11 | Online + In Person Take your Phase 1 MVP and turn it into a functioning AI-native startup. You can build more then 5 agents now. During Phase 2: Build and connect your AI organization Improve the product Launch and test with users Execute your GTM strategy Collect feedback and iterate Prepare an investor-ready pitch October 11 — Final Demos & Review Teams can present in person at participating locations for final demos and judging. Final judging will consider the product, AI organization, execution, validation, GTM, traction, and final pitch. Phase 2 has its own prizes and awards. The Progression Phase 1: Idea → Validation → Simple MVP → Initial AI Team Phase 2: MVP → 5+ AI Agents → Working AI Organization → Users → Investor Pitch Sponsors & Tools Kylon Kylon helps you create AI agents that can run business processes. It makes it easier to connect data, AI models, processing steps, and outputs into repeatable workflows. Check out https://cloud.rocketride.ai Prelint Prelint is your product whisperer, checking every pull request against product specs, business rules, and compliance requirements. It catches spec drift before code ships, turning product decisions into automated checks within your existing GitHub workflow so teams and AI agents can move fast without losing sight of what the product is supposed to do. Check out https://prelint.com InsForge InsForge is building agent-native cloud infrastructure for modern AI development. It brings together model gateway, compute, deployment, database, authentication, and more so AI coding agents can operate across the full development workflow. Check out the new product https://www.instacloud.com Voisekey Voiskey is an innovative AI voice research team dedicated to Expression Intelligence technology, focusing on the development of next-generation voice interfaces that comprehend a speaker's true intent. Check out https://www.voiskey.ai Querit Querit is a Web Search API built for AI. Powered by its proprietary global web index covering hundreds of billions of pages, Querit provides fresh, structured, and source-grounded web information for LLMs, AI agents, and applications. Learn more at https://www.querit.ai Paritok Paritok drops in and non-destructively compresses tools, files, and history on the fly for longer sessions and smaller bills. c0mpiled-18: YC Startup School Hackathon - Taipei Edition
📅 Wednesday, November 11, 2026 | 9:00AM – 7:00PM
📍 Location TBD
🍕 Lunch, Dinner, Drinks, and Snacks Provided | Free to Attend

🚀 Overview
Transpose Platform is excited to bring our c0mpiled hackathon series to Taiwan for the first time, just in time for the first-ever YC Startup School in Asia 💥
c0mpiled is a one-day, build-first hackathon: pick a topic from Y Combinator's Request for Startups, build on site, submit a 90-second demo, and get judged the way Silicon Valley judges early teams.
Since 2025 the series has run in San Francisco, Tokyo, UAE, Osaka, and Korea with YC alumni founders as judges and mentors at every edition.

🧩 Challenge: YC Request For Startups - Fall 2026
AI for the Aging Population — Max Kolysh
The Best Time to Build in Crypto — Nemil Dalal
New Operating System for the Physical World — Charlie Warren
AI Powered Consumer Products for a Billion People — Raphael Schaad
Proving You're Human — Max Kolysh
Multiplayer AI — Aaron Epstein

🎁 Prizes:
🥇 1st Place: Office Hours with YC Partner + $3,000
🥈 2nd Place: $1,500
🥉 3rd Place: $500
Winning teams also receive YC application mentoring from Transpose Platform and the visiting YC alumni founders.

🙌 Who should apply?
Engineers, designers, and researchers building with AI, in Taipei or visiting.
University and graduate students.
Aspiring founders and early-stage teams (pre-seed or seed) preparing for the US market.
You do not need a startup or a finished idea. You need to be able to ship in a day and present in English.

🤝 Team Format and Selection
Teams of up to 4, or solo.
About 200 participants will be selected from applications. Selection considers past experience and projects shipped.

💻 Rules and Submission
Build session: Existing models, APIs, and libraries are allowed; the product itself must be built during the event.
Submission: a 90-second demo video plus a live demo to peers during the judging session.
Judging: what was built during the event, product quality, and the team's execution speed and clarity.

About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!
